Build review · November 2

First Steps 0.1.5: the next headset test

Room-change recovery

Recenter/tracking-origin changes and an out-of-reach board trigger placement recovery. The old board hides, the session is held, and the placement prompt stays accessible. Old-anchor cleanup cannot restore the board to the previous room.

Test: move rooms during a game, recreate the boundary, place the board again, and compare the position and turn. Physical mode must require realignment. Repeat while a piece is held and during an AI move.

Fingertip grabs

OpenXR thumb and index joints now use the correct identifiers. Held pieces follow their midpoint instead of an incorrectly indexed palm joint. Invalid tracking cancels the grab safely.

Test both hands at different heights and angles. The grip must stay between thumb and forefinger, without drift or accidental commits.

Local Meta companion

ASK THE TABLE offers WHAT HAPPENED, EXPLAIN MOVE and HELP CONTINUE. Meta Llama 3.2 answers using supplied engine facts. The engine owns moves and history; replies cannot change them. Stale responses are rejected.

Button-driven text, not voice. The self-hosted launcher prepares local models and USB connectivity. Qwen camera recognition remains separate. No paid API.

Scene tests and an actual local Meta-to-Unity response passed. Real room/boundary behavior and fingertip alignment still need founder acceptance. Camera accuracy and full-scan speed remain open: the prior 64-crop synthetic workload took 30.7 seconds. Do not present this as seamless recognition.

Cerebral Valley sprint: today, tomorrow, submission

  1. Nov 2 — accept the core build. Install the exact 0.1.5 candidate. Test room recovery, both-hand grabs, all three companion questions, stale-response rejection, game over and PLAY AGAIN. Record failures against its fingerprint. Then run one continuous human → AI → virtual → physical route; label manual steps honestly.
  2. Nov 3 — make the demonstration reproducible. Fix only blockers on that route. Start the host from the documented launcher on a clean session. Have another person follow the quick-start without coaching. Record headset and real-board footage showing Meta assistance and unchanged game history. Retain an explicit manual fallback if scanning is unreliable.
  3. Nov 4 — submit and verify. Confirm the accepted participant rules, track and pre-existing-code requirements. Prepare the build, source, model attribution, equipment/setup instructions and demo links requested by the actual submission form. Test every judge-facing link. Submit by 2 p.m. Central and retain the receipt; 8 p.m. Central is the official cutoff, not the work target.
